themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints spiked to 18 this week versus a baseline of 2.0 per week—an 800% increase (z-score: 12.09)—suggesting a rapid emergence of Uber/Lyft congestion, illegal pickups, or related street obstruction issues in Washington Heights/Inwood this week.
evidence: 18 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Statistical z-score of 12.09 (extreme deviation, top decile)
No corroborating Reddit or local news coverage suggests sudden, localized emergence
reporting_angles: Interview 311 callers and residents on which streets are most affected; map complaint hotspots
Reach out to local business owners and TLC enforcement to confirm on-ground reality and any enforcement response

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments Triple
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 11 last week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 1000% spike (z-score: 7.56)—indicating a potential new or expanding homelessness encampment cluster in the district over the past 1–2 weeks.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with CB budget priority #1 on park safety and NYPD facility requests, suggesting chronic under-resourcing
reporting_angles: Locate and document the encampment(s): size, location, duration, services available (outreach, sanitation, medical)
Interview residents, service providers, and Parks/NYPD on response capacity and social services offered; frame as both humanitarian and public-order story

themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste Dumping
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints jumped to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 1100% increase (z-score: 4.16)—suggesting illegal dumping or environmental contamination emerging in Washington Heights/Inwood this week.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
No corroborating news coverage; localized, sudden emergence suggests specific illegal activity or site
reporting_angles: Identify the dumping sites via 311 complaint addresses; photograph and document environmental hazard
Contact DEP and NYPD environmental crimes unit to confirm investigation status; interview residents on health impacts

themes_detail.label: Tree Mortality Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints spiked to 3 last week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—indicating potential disease outbreak, drought stress, or infrastructure damage affecting street trees in the district last week.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Aligns with CB budget priority on park reconstruction and upgrades; suggests under-maintenance or environmental stress
reporting_angles: Work with Parks Dept. to identify affected tree species, locations, and likely causes (drought, pests, disease, construction damage)
Frame as climate resilience and urban forestry story; interview arborists on implications for neighborhood canopy and heat mitigation

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Drop
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints fell to 53 this week versus a baseline of 113.8 per week—a 53% decrease (z-score: -4.77)—suggesting either a sudden improvement in district sanitation or potential under-reporting/311 system issue this week.
evidence: 53 unsanitary condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 113.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Inverse signal: major anomaly but direction is positive; worth checking if real improvement or 311 artifact
reporting_angles: Verify with Sanitation Dept. whether this reflects actual service gains (new routes, equipment, staffing) or 311 reporting lag
If real: identify what changed and whether it can be replicated; if system issue: flag data integrity concern
